title: Product of Array Except Self
summary: Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] is the product of all elements in nums except nums[i].
statement: Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] is the product of all elements in nums except nums[i]. The product of any prefix or suffix of nums must fit within a 32-bit integer. Implement an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and does not use division.
constraints: nums contains 2–100000 integers from -30 to 30; every required prefix, suffix, and answer fits signed 32-bit.
Return at each index the product of every OTHER element in O(n) time without / or //. The output list does not count as auxiliary space.
reference_solution:
def product_except_self(nums):
    answer = [1] * len(nums)
    prefix = 1
    for index, value in enumerate(nums):
        answer[index] = prefix
        prefix *= value
    suffix = 1
    for index in range(len(nums) - 1, -1, -1):
        answer[index] *= suffix
        suffix *= nums[index]
    return answer
known_wrong_solutions:
def product_except_self(nums):
    total = 1
    for value in nums: total *= value
    return [total // value if value else 0 for value in nums]
def product_except_self(nums):
    answer = [1] * len(nums)
    prefix = 1
    for index, value in enumerate(nums):
        answer[index] = prefix
        prefix *= value
    suffix = 1

        answer[index] = suffix
        suffix *= nums[index]
    return answer
hints: The excluded-index product is the product to its left times the product to its right.
Write all prefix products into the answer, then sweep backward with one running suffix product.
Before multiplying nums[i] into the suffix, multiply answer[i] by the current suffix.
Zeros need no special case: prefixes and suffixes naturally propagate them. Do not divide.
editorial: The forward invariant makes answer[i] equal to the product strictly before i. The backward invariant holds the product strictly after i, so multiplying them excludes exactly nums[i]. The independent oracle constructs each answer by directly multiplying all other positions. The implementation uses only the output plus two scalars.

tests.explanation: For index 0 multiply 2×3×4=24; applying the same exclusion gives [24,12,8,6].
Only excluding the zero leaves a nonzero product, (-1)×1×(-3)×3=9.
